title: POC scoping - private networking & data residency (Sunset Health)
summary: POC scoping call to define success criteria, workload sizing, networking pattern (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency requirements, and a 4-week POC timeline. Customer needs SOC2-grade controls, KMS integration, and egress constraints for EU data. Agreed benchmarks and next steps: Redwood to share VPC diagram and security pack; Sunset to provide CIDR ranges and test account; run benchmark week 2, integrate week 3, review week 4.
topics: Networking options: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink
Data residency and egress constraints across us-east-1/eu-west-1
next_steps: Redwood: send VPC peering & PrivateLink network diagram + setup guide (Alex)
Redwood: share security pack (SOC2 docs, KMS/HSM notes) and benchmark spreadsheet (Priya)
Customer: provide CIDR ranges, preferred regions, and test account credentials (Tariq)
Schedule week 2 benchmark kickoff (calendar invite from Alex)
Decide on Dedicated vs Private deployment after benchmark
action_items: Alex Martin: Email VPC peering + PrivateLink diagram and step-by-step guide - due 2026-10-05
Priya Shah: Share security pack (SOC2, encryption, audit logs) and benchmark spreadsheet - due 2026-10-05
Tariq Rahman: Provide VPC CIDR ranges, acceptable egress endpoints, and test account by 2026-10-06
Maya Li: Confirm internal success criteria and list of stakeholders for the POC by 2026-10-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (CTO, Sunset Health), Maya Li (VP Eng), Tariq Rahman (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Alex Martin: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call - Alex from Redwood, Priya our solutions engineer - 
[00:08] Priya Shah: Hi all, excited to dig in.
[00:12] Jared Cole: Jared here, thanks. Maya and Tariq on our side.
[00:16] Maya Li: yep hi.
[00:20] Tariq Rahman: Hello.

[00:23] Alex Martin: Agenda for today - narrow the POC scope for private networking and data residency, agree on success criteria and benchmarks, and align on timeline and next steps. We got a few notes from your inbound: you want data to stay in EU when processing EU users, SOC2 requirements, KMS, and some egress constraints. Is that right, Jared?
[00:38] Jared Cole: Yeah that's right. Our main concern is we process PHI-like healthcare metadata. So we need control over where inference happens - ideally eu-west-1 for EU patient data, and us-east-1 for US. Also we have strict egress rules: any third-party endpoints must be approved or blocked.
[00:55] Priya Shah: Understood. For private deployments we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink patterns - peering is simpler if you want full network access, PrivateLink gives you endpoint-level control and avoids route table exposure. We'll walk through tradeoffs.
[01:12] Maya Li: Quick question - what about performance differences? We care about 95th percentile latency more than raw throughput.
[01:19] Priya Shah: Good point. In our experience peering typically has slightly lower added latency (single-digit ms), while PrivateLink has a tiny TLS hop and NLB in front which can add mid-single-digit ms. But queuing and batching in the runtime dominate in many cases. We'll benchmark both.

[01:40] Alex Martin: Let's capture high-level success criteria. From Redwood side we suggest: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms for 1-2 TB/day style workloads with average request ~120 tokens. Is that aligned with your expectations?
[01:55] Jared Cole: p95 < 400ms is ok as a target. Realistically, for some flows we might accept p95 up to 600ms if quality is better. But baseline needs to be consistent.
[02:05] Maya Li: We also need sustained throughput of roughly 60 QPS during peak, burst to 120 QPS for short windows.
[02:12] Priya Shah: Noted. Can you confirm average tokens per request and distribution - 120 average, 300 max?
[02:20] Tariq Rahman: Yes, around 90-150 on average, spikes to 400 in some analytics requests.

[02:35] Alex Martin: Ok, for sizing we'll propose a small Dedicated pool for the POC: 4 x A100-equivalent or 8 x T4-equivalent depending on quantization, with autoscale disabled for the test window so we can measure stable latency/throughput. That maps to about X tokens/sec - we'll put numbers in the benchmark sheet.
[02:56] Priya Shah: Also planning to run two variants: 1) hosted-private control plane with VPC peering to your VPC, and 2) Private endpoint via PrivateLink in your account. We'll run identical load for both to compare latency tail and egress behavior.

[03:20] Jared Cole: For data residency, we need logs and model inference to remain in-region. We prefer keys managed by our KMS and no model artifacts stored outside the region.
[03:30] Priya Shah: We support customer-managed KMS for the Private deployment. For Hosted we can restrict to region-specific deployment and configure our control plane to limit storage in region, but we need to validate audit trails. We'll include SOC2 artifacts and section on KMS/HSM integration in the security pack.

[03:54] Maya Li: On egress, we have a whitelist of endpoints. We can't have the service phone-home to unknown external endpoints. How does Redwood handle telemetry and health checks?
[04:03] Alex Martin: Good callout. For Private deployments and dedicated capacity we can disable non-essential telemetry and route metrics to your monitoring endpoints (Datadog, Prometheus) via approved destinations. The control plane can be configured to restrict outbound egress; we'll document that.

[04:25] Priya Shah: For the POC benchmarks, suggested tests:
- Warmed KV-cache runs vs cold start
- Sustained load at target QPS (60) for 20 minutes
- Burst tests to 120 QPS for 5 minutes
- Latency distributions (p50/p90/p95/p99)
- Token throughput (tokens/sec) and cost per 1k tokens
- Model quality spot-checks on 50 golden prompts

[04:55] Jared Cole: How do you suggest we measure quality? We have internal prompts and evaluation metrics; we'd like you to run Redwood's eval harness against our set and report regressions.
[05:02] Priya Shah: Absolutely - please share your prompt set and expected outputs. We'll run automated scoring and include a quality delta metric in the spreadsheet.

[05:18] Maya Li: Timeline - what's realistic for a 4-week POC?
[05:22] Alex Martin: Typical is 4 weeks: Week 0 (this week) - network setup and initial config; Week 1 - deploy POC infra, basic smoke tests; Week 2 - benchmark runs and data collection; Week 3 - integrate with your app flows and quality checks; Week 4 - review, tune, and final decision. We can compress if your team can provide CIDRs and test accounts immediately.
[05:44] Tariq Rahman: We can provide CIDR ranges and a test account by Tuesday.
[05:48] Jared Cole: We'll also need the network diagram and an explicit PrivateLink vs peering pros/cons doc for our security review.
[05:56] Alex Martin: We'll send both. Also we'll include a checklist for firewall rules and route tables.

[06:06] Priya Shah: A couple of technical notes: for large context models we recommend enabling KV-cache and setting batching to a 16-32 token window to balance latency/cost. Quantized model variants can reduce footprint but may impact some quality-sensitive prompts - we'll test quantized vs fp16.
[06:25] Maya Li: Do you have guidance for sequence length and memory for the dedicated pool sizing?
[06:30] Priya Shah: Yes - if 95% of requests are under 512 tokens, a smaller GPU mix is fine; if you see >1k frequently you'll need a larger GPU or different memory layout. We'll include a recommended sizing table in the sheet.

[06:50] Alex Martin: Regarding compliance, we will provide SOC2 docs and details about audit logs. For Private deployments we can integrate with your SSO (SAML) and RBAC.
[06:59] Jared Cole: Good - security is non-negotiable. Also, we may want to run a brief penetration test on the PrivateLink endpoint - will that be permitted?
[07:07] Priya Shah: Yes, with notice and scope agreement we allow pentests on Private deployments. We'll coordinate with legal and our security team.

[07:20] Alex Martin: Cost expectations during POC - we'll give a rough estimate in the pricing note. POC will be usage + reserved instance for the dedicated pool. We'll attach an appendix showing cost per 1M tokens for the tested configurations.

[07:36] Maya Li: Any required firewall ports for PrivateLink vs peering?
[07:40] Priya Shah: Peering mostly needs internal ports for health checks and API traffic over HTTPS; PrivateLink will use NLB and TLS to the interface endpoint - standard HTTPS (443) outbound from your VPC to the interface endpoints. We'll provide exact port and CIDR info.

[07:56] Jared Cole: For region selection, we'd like the EU workload to run in eu-west-1 and US in us-east-1. Can you handle multi-region routing?
[08:05] Priya Shah: Yes, smart routing can pin EU requests to eu-west-1 and fallback to a compatible variant if capacity is constrained. We'll test region pinning during the POC.

[08:18] Alex Martin: Success gate checklist suggestion (short): network connectivity verified; benchmarks show p95 within agreed bound or documented tradeoff; quality delta acceptable; security docs signed off; and integration smoke tests pass. Does that work?
[08:31] Maya Li: That seems reasonable. Add cost delta to the checklist - we need a ballpark for production decision.
[08:36] Alex Martin: Will do.

[08:40] (brief cross talk, audio glitch)

[09:05] Priya Shah: Practical next steps: I'll upload the benchmark harness and the spreadsheet; Alex will email the network diagrams and PrivateLink vs peering doc; you'll provide CIDRs and firewall state, and we'll schedule the week 2 benchmark kickoff.
[09:20] Jared Cole: Sounds good. Also can you include a sample IAM policy for the test account?
[09:26] Priya Shah: Yes - we'll include a least-privilege sample IAM role for the interface and for any S3 access needed during the test.

[09:38] Maya Li: Anything else?
[09:40] Alex Martin: One more thing on audit logs - we'll show how the access logs can be routed to your S3 in-region and encrypted with your KMS. That meets your retention requirements.

[09:50] Tariq Rahman: For egress constraints - we need a list of all external IPs/domains Redwood will talk to during the POC.
[09:57] Alex Martin: We'll include that in the network pack. Most calls are to control plane endpoints and optional telemetry; if you disable telemetry it reduces external hosts.

[10:14] Priya Shah: Benchmarks we want to capture metadata for: request id, region, model variant, batch size, cache hit/miss, tokens in/out, and inference latency. We'll also produce cost per 1k tokens in the report.

[10:31] Jared Cole: Good - we'll share our golden prompt set and expected answers. We'll also identify 10 high-value flows to be included in the integration test in week 3.

[10:40] Alex Martin: Recap of agreed items: Redwood sends network/PrivateLink docs + security pack + benchmark spreadsheet; Sunset provides CIDRs, test account, golden prompts, and confirms internal success criteria; schedule milestone calls weekly. POC target: 4 weeks starting immediately after network setup.

[10:58] Maya Li: Thanks everyone, please send docs to our security alias security@sunsethealth.internal.
[11:03] Alex Martin: Will do. I'll send an invite for the benchmark kickoff.

[11:07] Jared Cole: Thanks - talk soon.

(meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains some OCR-like mishearings in a few places (speaker attribution approximated). References to product names may be slightly inconsistent in the transcript.
